subtopic: Handling a legal or tax notice
subtype: Approach: calendar reminders and a document folder [Action]
passage:
Tejas, it's Keerthana. Every notice date goes into my phone calendar the minute the letter arrives, and I add a second reminder a week before. That's the whole trick, honestly.
I used to feel my chest tighten whenever a notice landed. Once, a due date crept up on me because I'd put the paper on the fridge and forgot it. Since then, I keep a folder on my laptop called "Notices". Each reply I send gets scanned and saved there, with the date in the file name.
Last month a new notice came. I found last year's reply in two minutes, checked the date in the calendar, and answered in an hour.
It's boring. But boring is what I wanted.

qa.q: What is the name of Keerthana's folder?
How did Keerthana feel when notices used to arrive?
qa.a: Keerthana's chest tightened, which shows fear and pressure that the calendar and folder later eased.

qa.q: What could Keerthana do if a notice needs documents that are not in the folder?
qa.a: Keerthana could add a list of usual documents to the folder and ask the office or a qualified person about what is missing.

qa.q: Why might Tejas have wanted to hear how Keerthana handles notices?
qa.a: Tejas may have wanted a simple habit to copy, since Keerthana calls it a boring trick that works.

grounding: The monologue shows a person putting every response date in the phone calendar with an earlier reminder and keeping scanned replies in one folder.

subtopic: Handling a legal or tax notice

passage: I'm Bhavna, Sonali's flatmate, and I've watched her go from someone who lost tax papers under the sofa to someone with a folder. After last year's notice mess, she sat at the dining table one Saturday and made a folder on her laptop called 'Tax replies'. Inside, one sub-folder per year. She scanned every letter she'd had from the department and the reply she sent, and named each file with the date. Then she opened her phone calendar. For the reply due on 30 June, she put one reminder on 30 June and another on 15 June that said, 'Start reply today.' When a new letter came in November, she opened the folder, found last year's reply to copy the format, and was done in an evening. I can't say whether she still worries. She just doesn't look frantic anymore.

qa.q: What did the 15 June reminder say?
What does Bhavna's last line suggest about Sonali?
qa.a: Sonali seems calmer and more in control now, though Bhavna can't be sure what Sonali feels inside.

qa.q: What else could Sonali add to her system?
qa.a: She could keep a simple list in the folder of each notice, its due date and its status, so she can see at a glance what is still open.

qa.q: How might life as a flatmate change for Bhavna with this system?
qa.a: Bhavna no longer has to watch last-minute panics or searches under the sofa, so the flat stays calm when a letter arrives.

subtopic: Handling a legal or tax notice
subtype: Approach: calendar reminders and a document folder [Action]
passage:
Monday, in April. A notice asks Nazia to confirm her rent receipts by 20 May. She writes the date on a sticky note, which falls behind her desk. Her colleague Ira asks a week later, 'Did you reply?' She hasn't. She finds the note on 19 May and stays up past two, scanning receipts, half of which she can't find.
Saturday, the week after. Nazia opens her phone calendar and adds every date from the notice, each with a second alert ten days earlier. She makes a folder called 'Notices and replies' and scans the reply she sent, naming it with the date.
Thursday, in October. A new letter arrives. Her phone buzzes: 'Reply due in 10 days.' She opens the folder, uses the May reply as a model and sends it that evening. Ira grins. 'Look at you.'

qa.q: When did Nazia find the sticky note?
How was Nazia feeling in October when the phone buzzed?
qa.a: She was calm and ready, able to reply that evening instead of feeling the panic of staying up past two.

qa.q: What small step would help Nazia's system last for years?
qa.a: Backing up the folder and checking it once a year would keep old replies safe even if the phone or laptop changes.

qa.q: What is it like for Ira to see the change?
qa.a: Ira, who once had to ask whether the reply was sent, can now just grin, pleased and relieved for a colleague.

grounding: It shows a person putting response dates in the calendar with earlier reminders and keeping scanned replies in one folder, so the next notice is easy.
